speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a psychiatric condition and a new movement disorder; to help me understand what is happening, can you describe exactly how your movements have changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; since the risperidone was started two months ago and your psychiatric symptoms have improved, could you describe the specific type of movement changes you are experiencing, such as stiffness, tremors, or restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of your risperidone. Has this internal restlessness been severe enough to prevent you from sitting still for more than a few minutes at a time?

REQUEST TEST: Physical_Exam (for parkinsonism and dystonia signs)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Neurological Examination - Motor: Normal tone and strength in all extremities. No involuntary movements noted (aside from patient's reported inability to sit still with frequent pacing). Coordination: Normal. Gait: Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The neurological exam confirms normal tone and strength, which supports your symptoms being due to drug-induced akathisia rather than parkinsonism. Given your recent improvement on risperidone, is the restlessness affecting your ability to function in college or sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The exam findings are reassuring, and your history strongly points to drug-induced akathisia from the risperidone. To confirm the severity and rule out other metabolic causes before we adjust your medication, could you tell me if you've been experiencing excessive sweating, heart palpitations, or tremors alongside this restlessness? Also, do you have a family history of seizures?

REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel (check electrolytes and calcium)
REQUEST TEST: Drug_Screen (to confirm compliance and rule out other substances)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrolytes: Sodium 140 mEq/L, Potassium 4.0 mEq/L, Chloride 100 mEq/L, Bicarbonate 24 mEq/L; Drug_Screen: Negative for non-prescribed substances.

speaker: Doctor
text: The metabolic panel and drug screen are normal, which makes thyroid storm or substance withdrawal unlikely. Based on your history of risperidone initiation and the specific symptoms of inner restlessness and pacing, this is consistent with drug-induced akathisia. Are you currently experiencing any dizziness, blurred vision, or difficulty speaking to help rule out other neurological issues?

speaker: Patient
text: {'Psychiatric': 'Improvement in delusions, hallucinations, and paranoid behaviors since starting risperidone.', 'Neurological': 'No history of seizures, headaches, or previous movement disorders.'}

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of inner restlessness, pacing, and fidgeting appearing two months after starting risperidone, combined with a normal neurological exam and ruled-out metabolic/toxic causes, is classic for drug-induced akathisia. We have gathered sufficient evidence to make a diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia
